shortName: Boston University Aram V. Chobanian & Edward Avedisian School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: Rather than specific required courses we look for competency in Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Math, and the Humanities.  Competence is determined by a review of the entire academic record (including post bac and graduate work) and test scores.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Chobanian and Avedisian School of Medicine is committed to diversity among faculty and students. Programs for the recruitment and support of students from groups underrepresented in medicine are managed by Admissions and Diversity and Inclusion offices. All applications are submitted to Admissions.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student may petition for a leave of absence for academic, personal, financial, administrative, or medical reasons. All petitions for Leave of Absence are prepared in consultation with the Associate Dean for Student Affairs or her/his designee.  BUSM makes every effort to ensure that students are fully supported throughout this process and that they can look forward to a smooth return to school.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are more than 50 active student organizations at BUSM, including service-related activities, clinical and academic interest groups, as well as social and professional organizations. These programs are organized and funded through the Student Committee on Medical Student Affairs and the Enrichment Office. There are also numerous school-sponsored service learning and enrichment programs.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: BU Medical Center is a beautiful urban campus, shared by clinical, educational, and research institutions. The four-square-block campus, located in the heart of Boston, is accessible by public transportation and is within walking distance of residential areas, shops, and cultural institutions.  In addition students have the option to complete all or part of their third year at the BU Kaiser Permanente Regional Campus hospitals in San Jose and Santa Clara.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The Medical Student Residence (MSR) provides on-campus housing in modern, fully equipped 2-bedroom apartments at subsidized rent substantially below Boston market rates. Approximately 75% of entering students choose to live in the MSR.   Other students live off-campus in the neighborhoods of Boston. Rents range from $2000 and up, depending on location and number of roommates.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Chobanian and Avedisian School of Medicine has several opportunities for support for gender and sexual minority students. Several groups are available for students, for example,  BU Medical Campus Pride, Sexual Health and Medicine, and CAMED Service PRIDE.  The Boston Medical Center is also home to a robust multidisciplinary clinical center for transgender medicine and a transgender research group which can (like other centers and departments) provide mentorship and research opportunities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Disability & Access Services provides services and support to ensure that students are able to access and participate in the opportunities available at Boston University. In keeping with this objective, students are expected and encouraged to utilize the resources of Disability & Access Services to the degree they determine necessary. Although a significant degree of independence is expected of students, Disability & Access Services is available to assist should the need arise.  In addition to helping students receive accommodations, we also provide resources to the University community so that events and opportunities can be made accessible.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The Student Affairs Office staff includes a Wellness Coordinator who plans multiple events and programs to support student wellness. In addition, there is a student run "Wellness Initiative" which provides additional programming.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
We strive to promote overall well-being in an environment sensitive to all cultures and beliefs that is conducive to lifelong learning and the professional development of compassionate physicians. Students have multiple opportunities to take advantage of the wide range of student-run activities, volunteer programs, career planning, and support services.

Our students are highly engaged in both their studies and the life of the campus.  They tend to participate in multiple extracurricular activities including service and research and they see themselves as advocates for people and or groups that are struggling.  Most students live on or near campus and find that much of their socializing happens with classmates and other students at the school.

Our students are ambitious about their own careers but not at all competitive with each other.  Because students have a wide range of future goals and plans, they are ready and able to support each other academically and socially.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students find it very helpful to have a car for away rotations.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Appropriate, professional attire is expected in clinical areas.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Chobanian and Avedisian School of Medicine is committed to promoting academic success for all students, with full-time professional learning specialists and tutors available for everyone.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Begins in Doctoring in the first week of first year.  Generally, students have one required session with patients per week in the first two years and then during the entirety of 3rd year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Curriculum is taught using an interactive flipped classroom modality that includes small group class discussion, team-based learning sessions, and laboratory exercises.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Doctoring includes a half-day/week session with patients in the 1st year and extends through the 1st 2 years. Formal, full-time clerkships begin in the 3rd year.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is required at most classroom sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The pre-clerkship curriculum runs from August of year 1 to the beginning of February year 2, and includes 3 courses:  PICIES, the integrated, body-system focused basic science course, Doctoring, the clinical skills course, and LEADS, which combines medical-adjacent didactics like research methods and advocacy with experiential learning and project work in an area of the student's choice.   The core clinical training includes all major disciplines, with ambulatory and inpatient experience in generalist and subspecialty venues. Some rotations take place at Boston Medical Center and some at one of our affiliates.  Elective blocks in 3rd and 4th years allow students to sample disciplines in a flexible manner. Research and international opportunities are available in basic science and clinical disciplines. Students may switch into several dual degree programs, and may choose a six to twelve month clinical block at BU Kaiser Medical (BUKM) in Santa Clara and San Jose, California.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Chobanian and Avedisian School of Medicine has, for decades, supported career goals in both primary care and in the sub-specialties.  There are primary care interest groups, a Family Medicine Scholars program, coordinated activities with primary care residency programs, opportunities for students to pursue longitudinal clinical training, alongside residents, in the teaching practices of our network of 15 affiliated community health centers, and an educational debt reduction program for students interested in primary care.  In recent years, 25-30% of graduates have pursued primary care careers.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: ​Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine (BUSM) is a leading institution in medical research, with substantial funding supporting its basic science departments.  The School of Medicine supports all aspects of biomedical research, from exploration at the basic science level to translating fundamental discoveries into treatments that improve human health. This has made us a leading institution with a focus on both traditional and interdisciplinary research. In recent years, approximately 85% of School of Medicine students have done significant research during their time in medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Many students choose elect to participate in on-campus and community based  programs serving disadvantaged communities.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Most clinical training is done at Boston Medical Center, our on-campus, principle teaching hospital.  All students have core and elective clinical opportunities throughout our network.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail for the first 2 years and then Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail for the clinical years.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Our tradition of social justice and focusing on patients go back a long way.  The New England Female Medical College was founded in 1848 as the first institution in the United States to offer medical education to women. In 1873 Boston University acquired the buildings and endowment and the school name was changed to Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine. This school was one of the first to connect the study of medicine with the care of patients, integrating clinical practice, education, and research.  Boston Medical Center, our primary teaching hospital, is combined with 12 neighborhood health centers (Boston HealthNet) to ensure "Exeptional Care Without Exception".  Chobanian & Avedisian SOM and BMC have strong cultural and institutional commitments to serving all members of our society, and these commitments are apparent in our clinical, educational, and research programs.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine is dedicated to the educational, intellectual, professional, and personal development of a diverse group of exceptional students, trainees, and faculty who are deeply committed to the study and to the practice of medicine, to biomedical research, and to the health of the public. We, as a community, place great value on excellence, integrity, service, social justice, collegiality, equality of opportunity, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Chobanian & Avedisian SOM is a social justice medical school.  This emphasis on social justice is evident in our curriculum and extra-curricular activities for students, in our faculty’s areas of research and expertise, and in the patients we take care of.

Curriculum and Student Activities
Our curriculum was updated several years ago to emphasize patient context and social determinants of health. In the classroom, our patients are never simply a patient with a disease, they are a person with a family who lives in a specific place and does a certain type of work…in the clinical setting, our students learn to address each patient’s upstream health needs as well as their acute medical needs; because we’ve learned that the best medical care in the world will fail to make patients healthier if they still lack food, housing, etc.  Outside the classroom, our students’ most common activity is to participate in some of the 17 or so service learning groups, which range from the “Outreach Van” street medicine initiative to the “Teen and Tot” facilitated support group for young parents to the Socially Responsible Surgery Club which allows students to visit surgical patients pre-discharge to ensure their understanding of their surgical problem and procedure and plan for follow-up.

Faculty Research and Expertise
A unique feature of our social justice medical school is that we are in the context of a Tier 1 research university.  While our research enterprise is very broad, you see the social justice mission thriving there as well.  Examples include the Grayken Center for Addiction, which supports research, education and treatment in addition medicine, in the Health/Care Disparities Research Program within internal medicine, and the Boston SOAR (Surgical Outcomes Analysis and Research) which investigates inequalities in surgical care.  85% of our medical students engage in Research during their time at Chobanian & Avedisian SOM.

Patient Population
Chobanian & Avedisian SOM’s primary teaching hospital is Boston Medical Center, which serves a primarily under-served and extraordinarily diverse patient population.  More than half of our patients are from vulnerable populations who rely on Medicaid and/or medicare for their health insurance; and 32% don’t speak English as their primary language.   Through our 12 affiliated neighborhood health centers, we reach deep into the communities of Boston to find the patients that need us the most.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Letters require institutional letterhead and handwritten signatures.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Please submit either one committee letter/packet letter (prepared by your pre-health advisor or committee) or three (3) individual letters.   We suggest that individual letters be submitted by persons who know you well “as a person” and who are able to describe the unique qualities you possess that will help you to be successful in navigating our curriculum and the medical profession.  Letters may be written by faculty members, supervisors for work or volunteer experiences, coaches, etc.  MD-PhD applicants should provide at least one letter from a research mentor for a total of (4) four letters.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: We require three virtual activities which may be scheduled on the same or different days: an interactive orientation to the school with the Associate Dean of Admissions, an individual faculty interview and a student-run information session.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews are required with at least one faculty member.  These are by invitation only.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: This binding program is typically reserved for candidates with extraordinarily strong academic records as well as some special or extenuating circumstance.  Contact Admissions for more information.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Chobanian & Avedisian SOM has extremely limited financial resources for DACA status students.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The Admissions Committee evaluates each application with a rigorous holistic review.  We will base our interview decisions on a review of the entire application; however a final admissions decision will not be made without an MCAT score on file. The CAMED supplemental application will be sent to all applicants who express interest after completing the AMCAS application, and should be submitted as early as possible, even if an MCAT test or score is not currently available.  Using holistic review, we will continue to evaluate each application individually for core competencies desired in medicine and that align with the mission of Chobanian & Avedisian SOM.

Applicants are expected to earn a bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university that is located in and accredited in the U.S. or Canada.  Applicants who have not graduated from an accredited U.S. or Canadian institution, but who completed a minimum of two (2) years in such an institution, including all of the prerequisites, may be considered to be eligible and should bring the details of their record to the attention of the Committee on Admissions. 

Applicants currently enrolled in a professional or graduate school program must be in the terminal year of the degree program to be considered for admission to the first year class.   Applicants must complete all requirements for any academic program in which they are enrolled prior to matriculation.

Individuals who have previously matriculated at another medical school are not eligible to apply.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Chobanian & Avedisian SOM utilizes a holistic review process whereby all applications are considered in their entirety.

Chobanian & Avedisian SOM utilizes a holistic review process whereby all applications are considered in their entirety.  The Committee looks for evidence of solid  knowledge in the basic sciences as evidenced by a combination  of academic work, test scores, and other relevant experiences.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours to consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework.  Chobanian & Avedisian SOM utilizes a holistic review process whereby all applications are considered in their entirety.  The Committee looks for evidence of solid  knowledge in the basic sciences as evidenced by a combination  of academic work, test scores, and other relevant experiences.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We prefer coursework be taken at a four-year college or university.  Other types of courses will be considered on a case by case basis.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Candidates are welcome to submit updates to their application and/or letters of interest throughout the application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine requires MD graduates to demonstrate a predictable level of competence across the knowledge and skills expected of physicians so patients, residency programs, licensing bodies, and others can rely on them. The school aims to provide a broad foundation preparing students for postgraduate training in any specialty.

Students must demonstrate proficiency, with or without reasonable accommodations, in all degree requirements. Accommodations enable meeting standards but do not provide cognitive support, replace essential clinical skills, or remove core curricular elements. Students must communicate effectively in urgent clinical situations and respond unassisted to alarms.

Technical standards require abilities in observation, communication, sensory and motor coordination, intellectual and quantitative reasoning, and appropriate behavioral and social attributes. Misrepresentation of abilities is a breach of professional conduct.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Chobanian and Avedisian School of Medicine is committed to ensuring that all accepted students can secure adequate financial resources; need-based aid is available in all years and financial need is not considered in the admissions process. The Student Financial Services administers its portfolio of scholarships and loans, assists students in securing aid from outside sources, conducts financial literacy and debt management seminars, offers entrance and exit counseling, and provides student financial management information.  There are no special institutional financial funds for international students. Unless an international student has an I-551 or I-151 resident alien card, federally insured loans are not available. Students may secure private educational loans with a co-applicant who is a creditworthy U.S. citizen or resident alien.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: BUSM has made a concerted effort to moderate the cost and debt faced by our students.  Tuition is set on an annual basis, at the minimum level that will support the ongoing commitments the school has made to students.  In several of the most recent years our rate of increase in scholarships and grants in aid has exceeded the rate of increase in tuition, resulting in a decline in the average level of indebtedness among graduates.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Wait List offers are extended by telephone and applicants are given a time-frame by which a decision must be made. Financial Aid offers made available during this time to help with decision-making.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants are expected to have demonstrated competence in foundational lab sciences including biology, chemistry, and physics, in the humanities and social sciences, and in advanced written communication.  Competence in these areas is often demonstrated by strong performance in biological sciences (i.e., biology, anatomy, cell biology), chemistry (i.e., general chemistry, organic chemistry, biochemistry), and physics.  Other related courses of study that may demonstrate competence in these areas will be considered on a case-by-case basis.  Applicants are also encouraged to explore these and other areas of interest through research, extracurricular activities, volunteering and employment opportunities.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Committee on Admissions conducts a comprehensive, flexible, holistic review of all applicants, striving to bring together a diverse student body comprised of academically gifted, highly motivated, resilient students who share a deep commitment to the values and goals of our profession and our institution.  This review focuses on each individual applicant's talents, accomplishments, experiences, and potential to contribute to the learning community; drawing upon information from the academic record, life history, recommendations, essays, and interview.  Personal interviews are required and are offered at the discretion of the Committee on Admissions.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: It is recommended that applicants display a reasonable understanding of the commitment and rigor required to succeed in the field of medicine.  This may be demonstrated in many ways including shadowing physicians, volunteer work, and paid clinical work.
